name: Pellucid BioSync Augmentation Surgeon's Full Kit
description:
Sterile pearl-white surgical gown in Pellucid's BioSeal nano-weave, sealed at every seam and rated for chrome-implant theatres. Beneath it: a form-fitting antimicrobial underlayer in pale silver. The gown's wide back panel accommodates spinal rigs without breaking sterility. Hands covered by Pellucid's tactile-translucent smart-gloves that transmit haptic feedback through chrome fingers. Soft-soled mag-cling surgical shoes in matte white. A BCI-linked heads-up visor sits across the brow, projecting patient schematics.

Used in licensed gene clinics and chrome-implant theatres across Tiers 3–5. The visor is the giveaway — street ripperdocs covet salvaged units and can rarely afford the real thing.
functionality: Full sterile-field rated construction, haptic chrome-compatible gloves, spinal rig accommodation in back panel, BCI patient-schematic visor, mag-cling non-slip soles.
what_it_says: This person has the legal authority and technical skill to open you up and put something better inside.
story_hooks: A street ripperdoc on the Shelf is wearing a convincing counterfeit of this kit — but the BCI visor is a dead prop, painted to look active.
The surgical gloves log every procedure to a Pellucid cloud server; a surgeon needs someone to scrub six months of records before an audit.
A patient woke up mid-procedure and saw something in the surgeon's visor display that wasn't part of their chart.

physical_description.visual_profile: A clinical, ethereal silhouette — pearl-white surgical gown with a commanding presence. The wide back panel creates subtle asymmetry when worn, suggesting anatomical accommodation for augmentation work. The outfit reads as both sterile precision and underlying danger: a uniform of intimate chrome-work and body modification. Paired with translucent smart-gloves and a low-slung BCI visor, the wearer becomes part instrument, part oracle.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through torso with strategic compression at wrists and ankles. The gown drapes with controlled flow, never clinging except where sealed. The underlayer is second-skin tight, creating a layered silhouette. Shoulders remain broad and unencumbered for surgical reach. Footwear is minimal — mag-cling keeps the wearer anchored to conductive theatre floors.
physical_description.primary_material: BioSeal nano-weave (primary gown), antimicrobial smart-fabric underlayer, translucent haptic-conductive polymer (gloves), mag-adhesive sole composition (shoes)
physical_description.texture: Gown: smooth, almost liquid-like pearl finish with imperceptible seam-sealing. Underlayer: soft ribbed compression texture. Gloves: translucent with micro-tactile node grid visible under light. Shoes: matte, non-reflective, slightly grippy.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant pearl-white with pale silver underlayer visible at neckline and wrists. Visor trim in surgical blue accent. BCI interface glows soft cyan when active.
closures: Magnetic snap-clasps down front of gown (sealed when fastened)
Mag-cling shoes adhere to conductive flooring without fasteners
distinctive_features: Wide back panel extending 20cm lower than standard surgical gown — designed for spinal rig accommodation without compromising sterility
Full seam-sealing throughout; no exposed stitching
Smart-gloves with visible haptic node grid across palm and fingertips for chrome-interface feedback
Integrated BCI-linked heads-up visor with patient schematic projection capability
Pellucid branding embossed subtly at left shoulder in matte finish
Underarm ventilation ports sealed with nano-mesh (invisible unless inspected)
Soft-soled mag-cling shoes leave no contamination residue
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1–2 genuine units (licensed clinics); Tier 3 institutional ownership; Tier 5 salvage knockoffs and ripped visor units on street ripperdocs
physical_description.cultural_context: The uniform of authorized augmentation surgeons, gene-clinic technicians, and chrome specialists. On Tier 5, a salvaged or counterfeited version signals dangerous ambition — someone operating without license in back-alley theatres. The visor especially marks the wearer as someone who interfaces directly with augmentation systems, making them simultaneously healer and hacker in the eyes of the street.
physical_description.condition_typical: Genuine units remain pristine; they're replaced seasonally for sterility. Salvaged versions show micro-wear, faint staining that won't come out, and visors with cracked displays or lag in projection. Street versions are patchwork assemblies — real gown, counterfeit gloves, salvaged visor held together with friction tape.
